summary: Echoes of Exploration is an interactive, story-driven web museum built for school-age space enthusiasts. Instead of listing dry technical specs, it lets six iconic pieces of NASA hardware—left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space—tell their own first-person stories. Using real NASA mission data from Apollo 11, Apollo 15, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, and Voyager 1, young learners can explore where each machine rests, listen to read-aloud narration, compare off-world travel records, and test their knowledge with an interactive quiz.
details:
What does it do?

Echoes of Exploration transforms NASA's discarded and retired space hardware into an interactive, kid-friendly storybook. Students can filter artifacts by destination (Moon, Mars, Deep Space) or current status (Still Active vs. Resting Quietly), open first-person story cards with built-in Read-Aloud narration, explore an interactive distance-comparison chart and radio-signal delay simulator, and take a 5-question Explorer Quiz.

How does it work?

The application is a self-contained single-page web app built with HTML5, Tailwind CSS, vanilla JavaScript, Chart.js, and the Web Speech API (speechSynthesis) for accessibility and audio storytelling. All mission timelines, coordinates, driving distances, marsquake counts, and deep-space milestones are grounded in official NASA Science, JPL, and NSSDCA mission records.

What benefits does it have & what do we hope to achieve?

School-age learners often only hear about active launches, missing the incredible science still happening on "quiet" or decades-old hardware—like Apollo 11's 1969 laser retroreflector still bouncing Earth lasers today, or Voyager 1 reaching one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026. Our goal is to spark curiosity in STEM and show students that even retired spacecraft leave a lasting scientific legacy.

Tools, languages, and software used:

HTML5, CSS3 (Tailwind CSS), JavaScript (ES6+), Chart.js, Web Speech API, Python (python-pptx for the 7-slide demo deck), and SI-assisted illustration & drafting tools (disclosed below).
